card: Enables the -Wmissing-noreturn compiler warning in the build system and annotates non-returning functions, methods, and lambdas across the codebase with [[noreturn]]. This prevents compiler false positives where the compiler cannot determine that an execution path terminates, such as spurious missing-return warnings. The PR also replaces several bare exit() calls with std::exit() and ignores Clang C++23 lambda attribute warnings. Changes touch bundled dependencies including libmultiprocess and subprocess.h, matching upstream PRs.
evidence: PR description: "Missing [[noreturn]] attributes can cause compiler false positives and other issues; see discussion in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35896#discussion_r3726612556."
problem: Functions that never return (such as unconditional throwers, exit handlers, and fatal assert stubs) lack [[noreturn]] annotations, which can cause compiler false positives such as bogus missing-return warnings. Without an enforced compiler warning flag, newly added functions can easily omit the attribute.
scope_notes: Includes a temporary nomerge commit modifying libmultiprocess in-tree and modifies bundled subprocess.h, which correspond to upstream dependency PRs.
summary: Enables the -Wmissing-noreturn compiler warning flag in CMake and annotates non-returning functions, methods, and lambdas across the codebase with [[noreturn]]. It suppresses -Wc++23-lambda-attributes warnings when applying [[noreturn]] to lambdas under Clang, and adds diagnostic pragmas around build-dependent fuzz functions. Additionally, it converts several legacy exit() calls to std::exit().
